sources.entry: poorcoder - Lightweight Bash scripts that enhance your terminal coding workflow with web-based AI assistants like Claude or Grok.

summary.one_liner: poorcoder is a set of lightweight Bash scripts that gather project code context for pasting into web-based AI chat interfaces, apply code changes from LLM markdown responses, and generate AI commit messages from git changes.
summary.what_it_does: The repository contains four Bash scripts. 'context' collects code from selected files or glob patterns (with include/exclude options and optional git information) so it can be pasted into a web LLM. 'apply-md' reads markdown, typically an LLM response from stdin or the clipboard, extracts code blocks, and writes them to the filesystem, with dry-run, verbose, and create-missing options. 'git-context' produces git-related information meant to help an LLM write commit messages. 'autocommit' wraps git-context and the llm CLI to commit all changes with an AI-generated message, then opens an editor so the user can review it. The README describes a workflow where context is copied to a web chat, and the response is applied back to the project. The README also shows pipelines using the llm CLI with an API-based model.
use_cases: copy project code into a web chat like Claude.ai or Grok
apply code changes from an LLM response to local files
generate AI commit messages from git changes
preview LLM-suggested edits with a dry run
pipe file context into a command-line LLM for quick fixes
use a flat-rate chat subscription alongside terminal work
stack: llm CLI (optional, for git-context and autocommit)
notable: Designed for web-based LLM subscriptions instead of API-driven IDE tools
apply-md turns markdown code blocks from an LLM response into file changes, with dry-run preview
autocommit generates a commit message from git changes and opens an editor for review
Project-specific install option copies scripts and prompts into your own repo for customization
Released into the public domain under The Unlicense
caveats: clipboard examples use pbcopy/pbpaste (macOS); the README only names xclip as the Linux alternative
autocommit and git-context require the llm CLI installed and configured with a model, which implies API usage costs
The README describes scripts only and gives no test or maintenance information
